gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states that the "silent" switches are specified at different points and tolerances (Lofree Void 40±10 gf at 1.3 mm actuation, Cherry MX2A Silent Red 45 cN ≈ 45.9 gf at 1.9 mm, Gamakay Phoenix V3 45±5 gf at a fixed 2.0 mm), so their force ranges overlap and only travel separates them (2.8 mm vs 3.7 mm vs 3.5 mm).
standout_why: Compared against the two cited pages that rendered: mkbguide.com and keyboardranker.com. mkbguide already says decibel readings from different sources cannot be ranked against each other, says no maker publishes a dB figure for its picks, and tabulates force and travel for the Lofree Void, Cherry MX2A Silent Red and NuPhy Blush Nano. keyboardranker says its picks were not measured for sound and gives Cherry's 45 cN / 1.9 mm / 3.7 mm. So the core of this angle (maker noise claims are not comparable) is already in a cited rival. What they lack: any Hall effect silent board (no Gamakay Phoenix V3 row), the cN-to-gf conversion, and the point that tolerances make the force ranges overlap. Both cited RTINGS pages (best/quiet, best/work) returned only navigation in my reader, and I did not open the ten uncited results, so this score is judged against two pages only.
decides: It does not change the pick. It confirms that noise has to be ranked on one lab's measurements (RTINGS, which ChatGPT cited), not on maker labels: no decibel figure appears on the Logitech page, the Gamakay blog page, or the HLPlanet and Deskforged reviews I opened. The force figures cannot separate the three silent switches once tolerances are applied; travel can (the Void is the short-travel one at 2.8 mm). Among boards we link, the Lofree Flow 2 84 with Void switches is the one ChatGPT already names on RTINGS' authority and fits the premium low-profile segment. The Gamakay Phoenix V3 boards are the only silent boards we link at sale prices under $100 (per the supplied table), but I found no measured noise figure for them, so they can be listed on spec only, not ranked on noise.

findings.label: Normalised silent-switch force and travel (the footnote is the finding)
findings.value: Lofree Void 30-50 gf at 1.3 mm actuation, 2.8 mm total; Cherry MX2A Silent Red about 45.9 gf at 1.9 mm, 3.7 mm total; Gamakay Phoenix V3 40-50 gf at 2.0 mm, 3.5 mm total
findings.source_title: Best Quiet Mechanical Keyboards for the Office (2026) | MKB Guide
findings.note: Arithmetic: 45 cN × 1.0197 = 45.9 gf. Ranges are the stated tolerances applied (40±10 gf, 45±5 gf). Void and Cherry figures are as mkbguide states them; Phoenix V3 figures are from HLPlanet (next rows). Cherry's figure is at its 1.9 mm pre-travel, Lofree's at 1.3 mm actuation, Gamakay's at a fixed 2.0 mm because a Hall effect switch's actuation point is set in software. The three force ranges overlap, so force cannot rank them; total travel can.

findings.product: Gamakay TK75HE V2 / TK75 TMR / NS75 (Phoenix V3 silent switch)
findings.label: Switch force and travel as HLPlanet tabulates them
findings.value: 35 gf minimum initial force, 45 ± 5 gf at 2.0 mm, 58 gf maximum end force, 3.5 ± 0.2 mm total travel
findings.source_title: Review: Gamakay Phoenix V3 Silent Magnetic Switch (HLPlanet, Marcus Richardson, 2026-07-01)
findings.note: Same table lists Mercury V3 (the non-silent sibling) at 30 gf minimum, 45 ± 5 gf at 2.0 mm, 55 gf maximum, 3.5 ± 0.1 mm. Richardson calls the Phoenix V3 "slightly heavier at the bottom-out than the Mercury V3". The review has a sound-test heading but no decibel figure or method.
